title: Dual-mode application of transcriptional regulation and DNA editing using the ultra-compact TnpB system.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the 9.45 MB supplement. Opened all three Excel files: 'extended data file1' (9 small raw-data sheets, 183 rows containing numbers, 816 numeric cells total: fluorescence intensities and qPCR fold-changes), 'extended data file2' (3 sheets, only 85/73/37 non-empty cells - these are picture-holding sheets for gel and microscopy panels, not numbers), and 'extended data file3' (167,709 rows x 5 columns: chrom, pos, ref, alt, variant_type from whole-genome sequencing; 89,930 insertions/deletions and 77,779 single-base changes, with no efficiency or on/off-target label). Extracted text from all 57 pages of the supplementary PDF: its tables hold plasmid, primer, guide and predicted off-target sequences, not measured efficiencies.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the deposited sequencing (targeted amplicon, RNA-seq, whole-genome) lives in the three SRA BioProjects; I did not download raw reads (policy forbids fastq). The per-figure editing efficiencies and activation fold-changes quoted in the text (e.g. 0.61% and 1.37% homology-directed repair at two sites) were read from the article, not from a table.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement (9.45 MB zip, 3 xlsx + 1 PDF) downloaded and opened without login. Primary sequencing is open in SRA but is raw reads only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No column anywhere pairs a guide/target sequence with an editing efficiency or activation fold-change. The numbers sit in figure-shaped blocks labelled 'T1..T10' or 'OT1..OT9'; guide sequences sit in a separate PDF table. The feature-label table would have to be built by hand from figures and PDF text.

a3_inputs_present.note: Guide (omega-RNA) and target DNA sequences are present as text in the supplementary PDF for a few dozen sites; no accession lookups needed, but they need manual transcription from the PDF.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated per sheet (mean fluorescence intensity fold-change vs non-targeting control; relative expression 2^-ddCt; indel percentage), but the three readouts are on different scales and not comparable to each other.

a5_enough_rows.note: 183 rows containing any number across the 9 raw-data sheets, and these are experimental conditions with 3-4 replicate columns, covering on the order of 40 distinct guide-target combinations. Checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows (or ~400 for classification). The 167,709-row whole-genome variant list has no prediction target attached.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Whole supplement is 9.45 MB; everything opens in pandas/openpyxl instantly.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Sheet contents match the figure panels they are named after; the paper quotes no total row count for the variant list, so there is nothing to disagree with.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are direct physical measurements (flow/microscopy fluorescence, qPCR, targeted amplicon sequencing analysed with Cas-Analyzer); no model-derived labels. Only the off-target candidate lists come from software (Cas-OFFinder).

existing_models.name: TEEP (TnpB Editing Efficiency Predictor), a deep-learning guide-activity model from Marquart et al., Nature Methods 2024
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported correlation r > 0.8 between predicted and measured omega-RNA (guide RNA) activity; trained on a library of 10,211 measured target sites for ISDra2 TnpB. Split details not checked by me beyond the abstract-level description.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer of guide-design rules across TnpB orthologs and to complex genomic contexts; the follow-up literature calls transferable omega-RNA scaffold rules across orthologs an open problem.

existing_models.name: Web tools for TnpB guide design (tnpb.app; CRISPy-web 3.0 multi-modal guide design including TnpB)
existing_models.score_and_split: Web services; no benchmark number retrieved by me.

backbone.name: A DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 would be the natural backbone for guide/target sequence features
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for embedding ~40 short sequences, but 40 examples cannot train or honestly evaluate any head.
backbone.licence: Backbone licences are permissive/open; irrelevant here because the dataset is too small.

integration.partner_dataset: The 10,211-site ISDra2 TnpB activity library behind TEEP (Nature Methods 2024), joinable on 20-nt guide/target sequence and TAM (target-adjacent motif) context
integration.join_key: guide sequence + target-adjacent motif; genomic coordinates (hg38) for the human sites
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do guide-activity rules learned on one TnpB ortholog (ISDra2) transfer to a different ortholog (ISDge10)? - a good question, but this paper supplies only a few dozen ISDge10 measurements to test it with, which is too few to answer it.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the published mismatch rule: TAM-proximal mismatches abolish ISDge10 TnpB cutting while TAM-distal mismatches are tolerated (shown in the paper's Figure 6).
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling; not meaningful at n of roughly 40.
controls.external_validation: The TEEP training library (10,211 ISDra2 TnpB sites) would be the external set, but the direction of transfer would have to run the other way: train on TEEP's data and test on this paper's handful of ISDge10 sites, which gives a test set too small for a stable correlation.

honest_claim_h3: With the data in this paper, the only honest claim would be 'on roughly 40 guide-target pairs measured in one lab with one TnpB ortholog, a model ranks guides about as well as chance allows us to measure' - the sample is too small to support any statement about guide design.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use guide and target DNA sequence to predict how strongly a compact gene editor cuts or switches on a gene.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one guide RNA paired with its genomic target site, plus the guide length and the nearby motif. I counted about 40 distinct guide-target combinations with numbers in the supplement, across 183 condition rows.
plain_idea.predict: Two outputs: percent of DNA molecules edited (measured by sequencing the target region), and fold increase in gene expression (measured by quantitative PCR or fluorescence of a reporter).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs picking a guide for the compact TnpB editor currently test several by hand; a good predictor saves weeks of cloning. But that result already exists for a related TnpB protein, and this paper has far too few measurements to add to it.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes roughly 40 measured guide-target combinations for the ISDge10 TnpB protein; the existing TEEP model was trained on 10,211 measured sites for ISDra2 TnpB. We would have 0.4% of their data.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate measurements exist per condition, so noise is estimable in principle, but with ~40 combinations there is no way to produce a calibrated per-prediction confidence that would mean anything.

models_beatable.why: TEEP is a 2024 deep-learning model with a public web tool and reported correlation above 0.8 on a 10,211-site library; nothing in this paper's data could beat or even fairly re-test it.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The new data (this paper's ISDge10 measurements) comes from a different protein, different assays and a different lab than TEEP's library, so the 'same quantity measured the same way' condition fails, and the ~40 examples cannot shift a model trained on 10,211.

ml_idea: Considered: predict TnpB editing efficiency and transcriptional-activation strength from guide/target sequence, and predict the switch point between binding-only and cutting as guide length is varied from 8 to 20 nucleotides. Rejected: the paper is a small-scale engineering study, not a screen, and the measurements never exist as a sequence-to-efficiency table.

effort.compute_note: Everything here is tiny (9.45 MB supplement, largest table 167,709 rows x 5 columns, which pandas reads in seconds on this laptop - timed, not estimated). Compute was never the constraint; sample size is.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct guide-target pairs that have a numeric efficiency attached. I did it: about 40, across 183 condition rows, versus the ~1,500 the checklist requires. Ten minutes of work kills the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A2. The supplement holds 183 condition rows of fluorescence and quantitative-PCR numbers (about 40 distinct guide-target combinations), not the thousands needed, and no table anywhere pairs a guide sequence with its measured efficiency - that table would have to be reconstructed by hand from figure panels and a PDF. The only large file, a 167,709-row whole-genome variant list, carries no prediction target. Separately, the task is already served: TEEP (Nature Methods 2024) predicts TnpB guide activity at r > 0.8 from a 10,211-site library, with a public web tool.
